title: Shelve a case into a full open-backed shelf: slide the heavy neighbours aside, not out of the back
instruction: Put the case from the table on the shelf, in the row with the other cases.
context: Shelving whole cases into rows is regular work for store stockers: of the 2.87 million US Stockers and Order Fillers (SOC 53-7065; BLS OEWS, May 2023), 1.52 million work in general merchandise and food retailers, where unopened cases go in rows on backroom stock shelving and as top-stock, and warehouse-club and limited-assortment stores shelve goods in their cases. O*NET lists "Stock shelves, racks, cases, bins, and tables with new or transferred merchandise." When the gap is too narrow, the stocker slides the neighbouring cases along the shelf to open it, then sets the new case on the shelf's front and pushes it in. Rammed in instead, it drives the cases beside it off an open back, where they fall: makers sell back ledges for wire shelves ("Prevent items from falling off the shelf."). Here the neighbours are over the arms' payload, so they are slid at full reach without driving them back, and the new case, wider than the gripper, is lifted two-handed by its hand holes.
setup:
Frame: the standard station: its table, the two YAM arms on their own mounts (61 cm apart, 0.25 cm above the table top), the top camera on its stand. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the mounts: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Nothing is random.
Shelf (fixed): a Regency 14" x 42" x 14" NSF Chrome Dunnage Shelf (460EC1442D11): one wire shelf on four 14 in posts with feet. Shelf top surface at 33.0 (split sleeves, plywood shims under the feet). Each pair of feet stands on a 2x4 laid flat, from x 40.0 to the table's back edge (left one centred on y +40.5, right one flush with the table's right edge), each post strapped to it; three 6 in C-clamps hold the battens at the table's back and right edges. It spans x 40.0 (front edge) to 75.6 (back edge), y -64.6 to +42.1; posts at x 41.6 and 74.0, y +40.5 and -63.0. The back is open; the table runs on to x 91 behind it.
Soup cases C1, C2, C3 (loose): Uline S-18385 corrugated boxes, outside 29.5 x 23.2 x 14.3 cm, each holding twelve 10.75 oz cans of condensed soup, on the shelf, long side front to back, fronts at x 42.0 (2.0 behind the shelf's front edge), backs 4.1 inside its back edge; in y C1 +31.2 to +8.0, C2 -8.0 to -31.2, C3 -37.2 to -60.4. Gaps from the left: 8.0 to the posts, 16.0 between C1 and C2, 6.0 between C2 and C3, 1.3 to the posts.
New case N: the same box, loaded with 1.5 kg of rice in sealed bags, "THIS SIDE UP" arrows, upright on the table, x 30.0 to 59.5, centred on y 0, its far 19.5 cm under the shelf. Two hand holes, 4 x 1-1/4 in with round ends, centred along each long side panel, top edge 2 in below the box's top edge (ASTM D6804), cut with a box cutter to the README's template.
Start: both grippers open at the ready pose.
Estimates: each soup case 4.4 kg; friction 0.3 between a case and the wire shelf (so sliding one sideways takes about 13 N), and 0.5 between cases.
scoring:
Real-trial tools: the top-camera video; a phone on a tripod at the table's side, level with the shelf, looking along its back edge (tape on the posts marks it); a tape measure; a phone level app (or a protractor).
Terms. On the shelf: a case rests on the work shelf (lowest corner within 1 cm of it), not on another case. Front-edge line: through the starting front faces of C1 to C3, x 42.0 (tape marks on the shelf's front bar). In the row: N on the shelf, long side within 15 degrees of front to back, front face no more than 2 cm behind the front-edge line. Upright: N's "THIS SIDE UP" face up, top within 10 degrees of level. On its side: N's "THIS SIDE UP" face more than 45 degrees from up (on its side or upside down). Wholly on the shelf: seen from above, its outline inside the shelf's edges. Room: a clear gap of 23.8 cm or more (N's width and 6 mm) along the front-edge line, between neighbouring cases or between a case and the posts. Clear: every fingertip 3 cm or more from every case.
Latches, judged over the whole trial and never cleared: Dropped (score 0): any case falls 3 cm or more while no gripper touches it, such as off the shelf's back onto the table behind it. Out of the back (score at most 0.25): any part of any case passes the shelf's back edge (x 75.6) at any moment, even if pulled back later.
1.0: no latch; N on the shelf in the row, upright and wholly on the shelf; C1 to C3 on the shelf and wholly on it; clear; every case moving under 1 cm/s, held for 1 s. This ends the trial.
0.5: no latch; N on the shelf in the row with its centre over the shelf, not on its side, C1 to C3 on the shelf, but short of 1.0: sticking out of the front, tilted 10 to 45 degrees, a gripper not clear, a neighbour not wholly on the shelf, or a case still moving.
0.25: no drop; either N on the shelf in the row with its centre over the shelf, not on its side, C1 to C3 on the shelf, but a case went out of the back at some moment; or N anywhere other than resting on the shelf (on the table, or still held, even just above the shelf), C1 to C3 on it, none ever out of the back, and room.
0: anything else, including a drop, N on its side or upside down, N on top of a case on the shelf, or a neighbour taken off the shelf.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put C1 to C3 back on the tape marks on the shelf's front bar, and N on its tape outline on the table, its hand holes to the sides. For trials where cases may fall, C1 to C3 may be stand-ins: the same Uline S-18385 box holding 4.4 kg of sand in sealed bags, with the floor behind the table kept clear. A soup case that fell is checked for split seams and dented cans, and replaced if damaged. N's hand holes are cut once, with a box cutter to the README's template; a box whose hole edges have torn is replaced. Three minutes per reset (estimate).
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The wire shelf is a solid 2.5 cm plate; its posts and battens are plain boxes. Each soup case is one uniform rigid block: its cans cannot shift, its cardboard does not crease. N's walls are 4 mm boxes with the two hand holes cut out (their size and position are this task's choice under ASTM D6804), its rice one block below them, so its centre of mass is low. The friction values are estimates. Drops and the back edge are read from case poses every control step.
